Sovereignty of the People and Supremacy of this Constitution

Kiswahili: Mamlaka ya Wananchi na Ukuu wa Katiba Hii

Declares that all sovereign power belongs to the people of Kenya, to be exercised directly or through democratically elected representatives. Establishes the Constitution as the supreme law binding all persons and State organs.

Key constitutional takeaways

  • •All sovereign power belongs to the citizens of Kenya.
  • •Any law or conduct inconsistent with the Constitution is void.
  • •Every citizen has a duty to respect, uphold, and defend the Constitution.

Articles in Chapter 1

Select an article to read its legal clauses and plain language meaning.

Clauses

(1)All sovereign power belongs to the people of Kenya and shall be exercised only in accordance with this Constitution.
(2)The people may exercise their sovereign power either directly or through their democratically elected representatives.
(3)Sovereign power under this Constitution is delegated to the following State organs, which shall perform their functions in accordance with this Constitution- (a) Parliament and the legislative assemblies in the county governments; (b) the national executive and the executive structures in the county governments; and (c) the Judiciary and independent tribunals.
(4)The sovereign power of the people is exercised at- (a) the national level; and (b) the county level.

In plain language

Citizens hold the ultimate authority in Kenya. Leaders and State officers are caretakers delegated to serve under strict constitutional limits.
